provides: Cart, checkout and orders over opaque purchasables. A host registers what can be bought (purchasable_type -> a keyed-batch resolver Function answering title, price, currency, availability); the cart snapshots each line when it is added, so reading a cart never calls the product owner. Checkout re-prices every line, refuses with the refreshed cart when anything drifted, and places an order idempotently on a client key, emptying the cart and announcing orders.order.placed with its lines. Orders follow a staff-driven lifecycle with buyer cancel and a full staff refund; payment is a provider seam (none, mock) whose outcome arrives as the orders.payment.completed fact (or the payment module's payment.completed). Checkout seams let commerce companions plug in without forking: ADJUSTERS price the cart (discounts, shipping, tax; a quote endpoint shows them before submit, order adjustments are snapshotted) and CHECKOUT_HOOKS reserve before the order is written, commit once it is placed and release on failure or cancel.

gates.behavior: true: POST checkout/ answers error.403.checkout_requires_account to a guest session; false: guests check out like anyone else.

curated.summary: Whether a shopper must have an account to place an order. true (default): a guest can fill a cart but is asked to sign in at checkout, and the guest cart joins the account on sign-in. false: guests can place orders too. Values: true, false.

gates.behavior: none: payment_status stays unpaid; mock: payment.completed is emitted in the checkout transaction and the consumer marks the order paid (system check E002 outside the prototype posture stage).

curated.summary: none (default): orders arrive unpaid and the shop confirms them by hand. mock: every order is marked paid at once with no money moving, for prototypes only. A real payment provider registers its own name. Values: none, mock.

extension_points.name: PURCHASABLE_TYPES
extension_points.summary: What can be bought. {type_name: {'resolve': '<comm function>'}} merged over the empty built-ins; None removes a type. The resolver is one keyed batch for every type ({keys} -> {key: {title, price, currency, available, max_quantity, seller_id, image, url}}), so a custom app registers its product type in about twenty lines and orders never imports its model.

extension_points.name: ADJUSTERS
extension_points.summary: Price adjustments at quote and checkout. {name: {'quote': '<comm function>', 'order': int}} merged over the empty built-ins, applied by order (discounts 100, shipping 200, tax 300). Each answers {adjustments, errors} for the cart and the client's opaque context (schemas/functions/adjusters.json); total = max(0, subtotal + adjustments). Any error refuses checkout, the quote endpoint shows it; a silent adjuster is error.503.adjuster_unavailable.

extension_points.name: CHECKOUT_HOOKS
extension_points.summary: Reservations around checkout. {name: {'reserve', 'commit', 'release': '<comm function>'}}: reserve before the order row is written (refusal or silence refuses the checkout), commit once it is placed, release on a failed checkout, on cancel, and for crashed checkouts by the hook sweep. Idempotent on (attempt_key, name); state kept per hook in CheckoutHookState (schemas/functions/checkout_hooks.*.json).

extension_points.name: PAYMENT
extension_points.summary: How an order is paid: a short name from the payment registry (none, mock, plus register_payment_provider names) or a dotted path. The provider starts a payment inside the checkout transaction; the outcome always arrives as payment.completed, which is the only path that marks an order paid.

extension_points.name: TOTAL_BASE_CONVERTER
extension_points.summary: Dotted path (amount, currency, base) -> Decimal | None computing Order.total_base for reporting. Default asks currencies.convert by name; no answer stores NULL, never a guess.

extension_points.name: STAPEL_ORDERS_CART_PRESENTER / STAPEL_ORDERS_ORDER_PRESENTER / STAPEL_ORDERS_QUOTE_PRESENTER
extension_points.summary: Swap keys (STAPEL_SWAP) for the cart, order and cart-quote response presenters, so a host changes what the API shows without forking a view.

extension_points.name: orders.order.placed
extension_points.summary: An order was placed; carries its lines (type, key, quantity, unit price, seller) and no personal data, so a product owner can decrement stock and a seller can be told.

extension_points.name: orders.order.status_changed
extension_points.summary: Every lifecycle move, with the actor (owner, staff, system) and an optional reason.

extension_points.name: payment.completed
extension_points.summary: Consumed: reference_type 'order' marks the order paid when amount and currency match its total, and sends it to needs_review when they do not.

surface.name: active_provider
surface.intent: The provider this deployment runs (orders_settings.PAYMENT).

surface.name: payment_completed_payload
surface.intent: Build the orders.payment.completed payload a PAYMENT provider emits when an order is paid in full (user_id null for a guest, simulated for test money). Reach for it in a provider instead of emitting the payment module's payment.completed.

surface.name: payment_names
surface.intent: The short names PAYMENT accepts; also the environment vocabulary.

surface.name: register_payment_provider
surface.intent: Register a payment provider under a short name PAYMENT (and the environment) may then choose. The provider starts a payment in the checkout transaction; the outcome arrives as orders.payment.completed (or the payment module's payment.completed).

surface.name: reset_payment_providers
surface.intent: Drop registered providers — a test lever.

surface.name: resolve_payment
surface.intent: Turn a PAYMENT value (short name or dotted path) into a provider; the AppSettings resolver for the key.

surface.name: get_purchasable_types
surface.intent: The effective registry (built-ins <- settings <- runtime). Ask it instead of reading the setting, which misses runtime registrations.

surface.name: register_purchasable_type
surface.intent: Declare a purchasable type and its resolver Function from an AppConfig.ready() (or a test). The registry ships empty; this and STAPEL_ORDERS['PURCHASABLE_TYPES'] are the only two ways in, and both replace hand-building a cart for a custom product. entry=None removes a type a lower layer provided.

surface.name: reset_purchasable_types
surface.intent: Drop runtime registrations, leaving settings untouched — a test lever. Product code calling it is undoing a registration that belongs in settings.

surface.name: resolve
surface.intent: Resolve keys of one type in one call through the transport, validated against the purchasables contract. Raises ResolverUnavailable instead of guessing; orders answers 503 on it.

surface.name: resolve_many
surface.intent: resolve() over (type, key) pairs, one call per type.

surface.name: resolver_name
surface.intent: The comm Function name that resolves a type, or UnknownPurchasableType.

surface.name: adjuster_entry_problem
surface.intent: Why an ADJUSTERS entry is malformed, or None; system check E006 asks it.

surface.name: build_request
surface.intent: The adjuster request for a cart's lines (currency, subtotal, lines with attrs, context); reserve adds adjustments_so_far and attempt_key to it.

surface.name: call_seam
surface.intent: Call an adjuster or hook Function and validate its reply against the seam contract; raises SeamUnavailable instead of guessing, which orders turns into a 503 refusal.

surface.name: get_adjusters
surface.intent: The effective adjusters (built-ins <- settings <- runtime) in application order; ask it rather than reading the setting.

surface.name: get_checkout_hooks
surface.intent: The effective checkout hooks in reserve order (release runs in reverse).

surface.name: hook_entry_problem
surface.intent: Why a CHECKOUT_HOOKS entry is malformed, or None; system check E007 asks it.

surface.name: is_guest
surface.intent: Is this user a stapel-auth anonymous account? Adjusters and hooks then see user_id null.

surface.name: parse_errors
surface.intent: Parse an adjuster's or hook's errors list into QuoteError values; malformed entries raise SeamUnavailable.

surface.name: quote
surface.intent: Run every adjuster in order over a request and return the Quote (adjustments, errors, floored total). Never raises: a silent adjuster becomes an error.503.adjuster_unavailable entry.

surface.name: register_adjuster
surface.intent: Register or override an adjuster at runtime (None removes) — a test lever and an escape hatch; companions register through STAPEL_ORDERS['ADJUSTERS'] in their settings fragment because they never import orders.

surface.name: register_checkout_hook
surface.intent: Register or override a checkout hook at runtime (None removes); companions use STAPEL_ORDERS['CHECKOUT_HOOKS'] instead.

surface.name: reset_seams
surface.intent: Drop runtime adjusters and hooks — a test lever.

requires.reason: comm bus (orders.* emits, resolver and status Functions, user.merged and payment.completed consumers), AnchorPagination, GDPR owner protocol, posture stage, AppSettings
the cart is keyed on request.user, and a guest is a stapel-auth anonymous account; user.merged folds a guest's cart into the account on sign-in
answers listings.purchasables, the resolver of the 'listing' purchasable type the stapel-shop preset registers
currencies.convert fills Order.total_base for reporting; without it total_base stays NULL
registers a discount adjuster and a redemption checkout hook through its settings fragment
registers a shipping adjuster; reads the delivery choice from the checkout context
registers a stock reservation checkout hook (reserve / commit / release)
